findings.title: [P1] Enforce research write scope outside the researcher's control
findings.body: The researcher has Write access, but this check compares only porcelain status entries. Rewriting an already modified source file leaves its ` M path` entry unchanged and passes validation. Additionally, the baseline marker resides in the exempt research directory, so a compromised researcher can rewrite it to match unauthorized changes even on an initially clean checkout. Prompt injection from fetched content could therefore cause source or configuration changes that research-end accepts. Enforce an exact report-path allowlist before writes and keep integrity snapshots outside the researcher's writable scope.

findings.title: [P1] Isolate probes from shared Git metadata
findings.body: A detached worktree shares repository configuration, hooks, and refs with the main checkout. A malicious build script executed by the probe can alter the shared Git configuration or install a hook in the common Git directory. Neither action changes main-tree porcelain status, so this helper returns success and worktree cleanup leaves the payload behind. Subsequent Git operations can execute that hook with the operator's privileges. Run untrusted probes in an isolated repository and sandbox that prevents access to the original checkout and its Git metadata.

findings.cross_file_justification: The only enforcement of the 'write exactly one file' rule is chart-ticket.sh op_research_end (lines 451-471), which compares git status inside the repo. Writes outside the repo root, to already-dirty tracked files, or anywhere under grimoires/loa/research/ are invisible to it. agent-types.yaml marks chart-researcher write_capable: true.
findings.description: The chart-researcher subagent is given WebFetch (untrusted internet content) together with an unrestricted Write tool. The constraint 'Write exactly one file: the report path' is prose in the system prompt only. A fetched page containing injected instructions can direct the model to Write to any path the harness allows: e.g. ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json to disable hooks/add a malicious hook, .claude/hooks/*, or a planted module. The post-hoc scope check in chart-ticket.sh research-end only diffs `git status` of the repository, so writes outside the repo, writes to files that were already modified before dispatch (status line unchanged), and any write under grimoires/loa/research/ (including other tickets' reports that are later inlined into the hand-off snapshot) pass undetected.
findings.failure_mode: Prompt injection from a web source leads to arbitrary file writes by a subagent that is advertised as 'read-only on the repo', including persistence via Claude Code settings/hooks that execute shell on later tool calls.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict Write at the harness level (a PreToolUse hook denying Write unless the path equals the dispatched report path), or drop Write and have the parent session write the report from the subagent's returned text. Make research-end compare a full content hash of the research directory and record a baseline of the home-level Claude config too.

findings.description: research-begin stores the pre-dispatch `git status` baseline at grimoires/loa/research/.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch and research-end (a) `comm`-diffs that file against the post-run status and (b) uses its mtime for `find .run .beads -newer`. The research subagent is explicitly permitted to write under grimoires/loa/research/, and research-end whitelists every path under that directory. So the subagent can Read the marker, make out-of-scope changes, then Write the marker back (refreshing its mtime and/or editing its contents) and defeat both checks. The 5-dispatch cap (op_research_begin counts marker files) is in the same writable directory.
findings.failure_mode: The scope check that is supposed to fail a research ticket when the subagent touched files outside the research directory can be neutralized by the very subagent it audits.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the baseline and cap counters outside any subagent-writable path (e.g. .run/ or a mktemp dir recorded by the parent), make it read-only, and compare content hashes rather than mtimes. Exclude only the exact report path from the 'bad' set, not the whole research/ directory.

findings.description: FR-1.1 now exempts `git branch -D spike/<slug>` when grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml holds a row with status decided, source grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md and a `to: decided` transition whose `by` starts with `operator:`. The ledger is a plain tracked YAML file that the agent can edit with Write/Edit (no Bash, so no hook) before issuing the destructive command. The `operator:` prefix is a free-text string, not an authenticated signal. The guard therefore trusts data the guarded principal controls.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or injected instruction) forges one ledger row and then force-deletes an unmerged spike branch, losing the prototype the guard exists to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Require an out-of-band signal the agent cannot write (e.g. the spike branch exists on origin: `git rev-parse --verify origin/spike/<slug>` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor spike/<slug> origin/spike/<slug>`), or keep the block and route deletion through the sanctioned prune helper.

findings.description: SP-1 is meant to stop spike content entering another branch, but several one-liners that do exactly that are not covered and some are explicitly allowed: `git checkout -B main spike/x` (create flags at line 855 cause `continue`, yet -B resets an existing branch to the spike head), `git push origin spike/x:main` (push is whitelisted by the comment and the merge regex at line 870 only matches merge|rebase|pull|cherry-pick), `git reset --hard spike/x`, `git branch -f main spike/x`, `git update-ref refs/heads/main spike/x`, and `b=spike/x; git merge $b` (the ref is in a different `;`-segment). The header lists some misses but not these high-impact ones; the gh-pr-create check also only looks at the local HEAD, so `gh pr create --head spike/x` from another checkout is caught but `gh pr create --base x --head feature` after `git push origin spike/x:feature` is not.
findings.failure_mode: Spike/prototype code is promoted directly onto main or the remote default branch, bypassing the review/decision gate the fence advertises.
findings.suggested_fix: Add patterns for `checkout -B|--force-create <existing> spike/`, `reset --hard|--merge spike/`, `branch -f|--force <name> spike/`, `update-ref`, and push refspecs `spike/<x>:<dest>` where dest != spike/<x>; document the remaining variable-indirection gap. Consider mirroring the same checks in run-mode-ice.sh.

findings.cross_file_justification: Reports in grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md are produced by chart-researcher from WebFetch output (chart-researcher.md). chart-ticket.sh op_handoff only applies the L6 sanitizer when inlining into the hand-off snapshot; the /chart command itself loads the raw files as context.
findings.description: The /chart command declares grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md as context_files, so every research report (content derived from arbitrary web pages) is loaded raw into the charting session, which has Bash and drives chart-ticket.sh resolve/close and the decision ledger. The 'untrusted data' purpose string is a label, not a sanitizer. The `> UNTRUSTED research output` first-line check in research-end only verifies a marker exists; it does not neutralize instructions in the body.
findings.failure_mode: Web-sourced prompt injection reaches a Bash-capable session and can steer decisions written to the ledger or trigger commands, before the operator reviews anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not auto-load research reports as context_files; have the skill read a specific report through the L6 sanitizer (context-isolation-lib.sh sanitize_for_session_start) when a ticket is worked, and quote rather than ingest.

findings.description: The build-path filter drops only objects whose `.issue_type` equals "question". chart-frontier.sh in the same change accepts `.issue_type // .type`, acknowledging br releases that emit `type`. On such a release, question beads (decision tickets) pass through get-ready-work.sh and become selectable build work, which is the exact outcome the change claims to prevent ('tickets cannot enter a sprint').
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous /run or /implement session claims and 'implements' a decision ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"` and add a test with the `type`-shaped fixture.

findings.description:
section_append passes operator/agent text via `awk -v line="$2"`. awk processes backslash escapes in -v assignments, so san1 (which strips control characters but not backslashes) does not prevent `
` from becoming a real newline. A --line/--why value such as `ok
## Not yet specified
- fake` injects new headers or bullets into the tracked map doc; injected fog bullets then block or alter handoff, and injected `## Closed` headers short-circuit op_close's grep.
findings.failure_mode: Map-doc structure manipulation through a value that looks like a one-line string.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the line through an environment variable (`line="$2" awk '... ENVIRON["line"] ...'`) or strip/escape backslashes in san1.

findings.description: `close --consumed-by <cycle>` is the one operation permitted unattended, but the cycle id is only regex-checked; nothing verifies that a PRD actually consumed this map (e.g. that grimoires/loa/prd.md cites the chart-<slug> snapshot or that the ledger/cycle exists). An unattended agent can therefore reject every open decision row, close all question beads and the epic, and mark any map closed by inventing an id.
findings.failure_mode: Operator's open decision tickets are bulk-rejected without a human present, abusing the unattended exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Require Status handed-off and a verifiable artifact (prd.md referencing the snapshot path, or a ledger row for the cycle) before allowing unattended close; otherwise fall back to the interactive-only path.

findings.description: The 'main tree unchanged' verdict is a `git status --porcelain` string compare. It cannot see: writes to the shared .git directory (the worktree shares it, so `git config core.hooksPath`/`core.fsmonitor` or a dropped .git/hooks/* persists and executes on the operator's next git command), further edits to files that were already dirty before the probe, or writes outside the repository. The header presents it as a guarantee that an unblock probe 'never writes App-Zone code in the main tree'.
findings.failure_mode: A probe command (possibly suggested by untrusted research) alters repo config/hooks or pre-dirty files and the helper reports success.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare `git config --list --local` and a hash of .git/hooks, include `git diff` hashes of dirty files in the baseline, and document that the check is an audit, not a sandbox.

findings.description: op_resolve sanitizes and URL-checks --name and --line but forwards --decision, --rationale, --evidence, --alternative-json and --answer-ref to dec-write-lib.sh decide untouched. These values land in decisions.yaml and are later rendered by `dw list --format md` into the hand-off snapshot that plan-and-analyze reads as priority-1 'settled' context. Multi-line or markdown-structured text (headers, fake `> UNTRUSTED` banners, URLs) bypasses the no_url/san1 policy the script applies elsewhere.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent sanitization lets structured or link-bearing text into the ledger and the priority-1 planning context.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply san1/no_url (or a multi-line variant that strips control characters and headers) to all free-text resolve arguments before invoking the ledger writer.
